question.text: Consider an <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>LC</mi></math> circuit, with inductance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>L</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></math> and capacitance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi></math>, kept on a plane. The area of the circuit is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>. It is placed in a constant magnetic field of strength <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></math> which is perpendicular to the plane of the circuit. At time <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>, the magnetic field strength starts increasing linearly as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>β</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">t</mi></math> with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>β</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>04</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The maximum magnitude of the current in the circuit is____<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math>.

solution.text:
Emf induced in the circuit is

E=dϕdt=ddtB0+βtA

=β×A

=0.04 V

So the circuit can be rearranged as

Using Kirchhoff's law we can write

E=Ldidt+qC

Ldidt=E-qC

For maximum current, didt=0, 

Or q=CE

Using work energy theorem,

qE=12Li2+q22C

At imax, CEE=12Limax2+E2C22C

Or, imax=CLE

So, imax=10-3×0.040.1×10-3=4 mA
